messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Two-storey rear extension with a new bedroom and bathroom", "project": "Semi-detached house in England", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "Sch 2 Part 7", "document": "BR2010", "text": "The extension of a building by the addition at ground level of— (a) a conservatory, porch, covered yard or covered way; or (b) a carport open on at least two sides;"}, {"ref": "para 2.2", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.2 Part P applies to electrical installations: a. in a dwelling-house or flat, and to parts of the installation that are: (i) outside the dwelling – for example fixed lighting and air conditioning units attached to outside walls, photovoltaic panels on roofs, and fixed lighting and pond pumps in gardens (ii) in outbuildings such as sheds, detached garages and domestic greenhouses. b. in the common access areas of blocks of flats such as corridors and staircases c. in shared amenities of blocks of flats such as laundries, kitchens and gymnasiums d. in business premises (other than agricultural buildings) connected to the same meter as the electrical installation in a dwelling – for example shops and public houses below flats."}, {"ref": "Sch 2 Part 6 para 1", "document": "BR2010", "text": "(1) A detached single storey building, having a floor area which does not exceed 30m2, which contains no sleeping accommodation and is a building— (a) no point of which is less than one metre from the boundary of its curtilage; or (b) which is constructed substantially of non-combustible material."}]}

message.content:
This needs a **building notice or a full plans application**, as the most likely route.

- **It is building work.** A two-storey extension is the "extension of a building" under reg 3. It must meet Part A (structure), Part B (fire, including escape from the new bedroom), Part L (energy), Part F (ventilation), Part G (the bathroom) and others.
- **It is not exempt.** The Schedule 2 Part 7 exemption only covers ground-level conservatories, porches, covered y
message.reasoning: This two-storey rear extension isn't exempt under Class VII, which only covers ground-level conservatories, and doesn't fall under Schedule 3 either. The Fire Safety Order doesn't apply since it's a single dwelling, so this needs a building notice or full plans submission, with full plans being somewhat more likely if there's a nearby sewer, though that isn't confirmed.
